audit.why: 52.42% over 1568 games with Rumble owning levels 1-3 and Malphite owning level 6 and first item matches the kits: Flamespitter is magic against a champion whose only pre-6 answer is Seismic Shard, and Unstoppable Force at 130s is the single event that flips it. EVEN at 6/10 is defensible; I put the real number in the difficulty text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text named 'Luden's or Shadowflame' as Rumble's first item while the full layer names Liandry's Torment, and content.whys[5]/mid named 'Iceborn Gauntlet' as Malphite's first item.
audit.why: Two different first items for Rumble across the two layers, and a specific enemy build I cannot verify from the local data.
audit.corrected: Aligned Rumble's first item to Liandry's Torment and replaced the named Malphite item with a generic first-item spike tied to what the kit actually does (armour scaling Ground Slam).

audit.whatIsWrong: Four things. (a) Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of Malphite's max health and only recharges if he has not been hit for a few seconds — Flamespitter is a 3-second continuous cone, which means it holds that shield permanently at zero. This is the single best interaction in the matchup and neither layer mentioned it. (b) Seismic Shard STEALS move speed for 3 seconds — he gains what you lose, so disengaging after eating it does not work; the page called it a plain slow. (c) Ground Slam deals damage based on his ARMOR, so his defensive stacking is also his offence — the page framed his armour as purely defensive and 'irrelevant' to the matchup. (d) 'Unstoppable Force is instant and undodgeable' — it is a 1000-range dash on 130/115/100s, and Scrap Shield absorbs damage but never the knockup.
audit.why: Riot text — Granite Shield: 'absorbs damage up to 10% of his maximum Health. If Malphite has not been hit for a few seconds, this effect recharges.' Seismic Shard: 'stealing Move Speed for 3 seconds.' Ground Slam: 'deals magic damage based on his Armor.' Unstoppable Force: 'launches himself to a location at high speed' at 1000 range.
audit.corrected: All four written in with numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.wants.you[1] read 'Double-Electro-Harpoon his slow Wind Wall'. Malphite has no Wind Wall and nothing resembling one. content.mid also said his W 'gives him bonus armor and attack damage', and that Unstoppable Force 'chain-CCs you through any silence window'.
audit.why: Wind Wall is a fabrication a player would look for and not find. Thunderclap's Riot text is 'attacks with such force that it creates a sonic boom. For the next few seconds, his attacks create aftershocks in front of him' — no armour, no attack damage. And the only silence in this matchup is Rumble's own Overheat, so 'chain-CCs you through any silence window' describes nothing.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall deleted; Thunderclap described as the on-hit aftershock cone it is; the silence line replaced with the real Scrap Shield limitation.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Auto-trade his passive' was listed as a common mistake with a generic 'that is his favourite window' body.
audit.why: It named no mechanic and gave no reason.
audit.corrected: Replaced with 'Let his shield recharge' — the actual recurring mistake, since stepping off him for a few seconds hands back 10% of his max health.

edits.before: At level 1 Malphite's Q poke is annoying but his armor is nothing yet — your Flamespitter deals magic damage that completely bypasses what he stacks, so walk up and Q him every wave. He cannot retaliate with a melee threat, and as long as you do not Overheat from sloppy Heat management the trade is yours. At level 2 your Electro-Harpoon turns the short trade into a shutdown: Q him, then fire both harpoon charges so he cannot close into auto range for his W proc, and walk away with the HP advantage. By level 3 the pattern is cemented — ride the Danger Zone empowered Flamespitter into double-E and he simply cannot tank your sustained magic output at low levels when his armor scaling has not kicked in.
edits.after: At level 1 Malphite's Seismic Shard poke is annoying but his armour is nothing yet — Flamespitter is magic damage, so walk up and hold the cone on him every wave. More importantly the cone strips Granite Shield: that passive absorbs up to 10% of his max health and only recharges after a few seconds untouched, so continuous burn keeps it permanently at zero. He cannot answer in melee, and as long as you do not Overheat by accident the trade is yours. At 2, Electro Harpoon turns a short trade into a shutdown — cone him, then spend both charges so he cannot close for Thunderclap's aftershocks. By 3 the pattern is set: Danger Zone cone into both harpoons, and he cannot tank sustained magic before his armour scaling arrives.

edits.before: Levels 4–5 are still a grind in your favor but Malphite's armor starts to matter: his W gives him bonus armor and attack damage, so if he ever gets an auto off your Flamespitter DPS drops more than it looks. Keep the wave near your side, force him to walk into Flamespitter range to CS, and never let him auto you for free. The Danger Zone window is still your best window, but respect that a chunked-down Malphite can still nuke you with a flash-R — if he drops below half health, ward the bush and do not get caught repositioning. At 6 the dynamic flips: Unstoppable Force is instant, goes through your Scrap Shield's movement speed, and chain-CCs you through any silence window, so play as if he might have R even if you saw it last fight.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay in your favour, but Malphite's armour starts to matter and not defensively — Ground Slam (7s) deals damage based on his armour, so the tankier he gets the harder his E hits back. Keep the wave near your side, make him walk into cone range to CS, and never hand him a free Thunderclap window. Remember Seismic Shard (8s, 625 range) steals your movement speed for 3 seconds and hands it to him, so disengaging after eating it does not work — leave before it lands, not after. At 6 the dynamic flips: Unstoppable Force is a 1000-range dash on 130 seconds, and Scrap Shield's speed burst will not outrun it while the shield absorbs damage but never the knockup.

edits.before: The late game is Malphite's — his armor scales into a wall against your physical teammates and his R is the most reliable teamfight engage in the game, but your Equalizer is the countervailing trump card. Position off the side so a Malphite R cannot hit both you and your carry, and use The Equalizer pre-emptively across the path where Malphite wants to walk in — the slow and magic AoE forces him to either engage through fire or abort. If you are ahead you can still burst him with a full-magic build before Unstoppable Force lands, but you need to be close to his flank before he targets you, not after.
edits.after: The late game is Malphite's — his armour is both a wall against your physical teammates and the scaling on Ground Slam, and Unstoppable Force is the most reliable engage in the game. Your Equalizer is the counter-card. Stand off to the side so one R cannot catch you and your carry together, and lay the burn line pre-emptively across the ground he wants to cross — the slow plus magic AoE makes him engage through fire or abort. If you are ahead you can still burst him before the R lands, but you have to be on his flank before he picks a target, not after.

notes: Biggest fabrication removed: content.wants.you[1] read "Double-Electro-Harpoon his slow Wind Wall". Malphite has no Wind Wall. Also removed: "his W gives him bonus armor and attack damage" (Thunderclap's Riot text is a sonic boom that makes his attacks create aftershocks in front of him — no armour, no AD), "Unstoppable Force is instant and undodgeable" (it is a 1000-range dash on 130/115/100s), and "chain-CCs you through any silence window" (the only silence in this matchup is Rumble's own Overheat, so the sentence described nothing). Named-item speculation removed on both sides: "Iceborn Gauntlet" for Malphite and "Luden's or Shadowflame" for Rumble, the latter of which also contradicted the full layer's Liandry's Torment. Best addition, and it was completely absent: Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of Malphite's max health and only recharges once he has gone a few seconds without being hit — Flamespitter is a 3-second continuous cone, so simply keeping it on him holds that shield at zero permanently. Second addition: Ground Slam's damage scales off his ARMOR, so his stacking is offence as well as defence, which the old text got backwards by calling his armour "irrelevant". Kit-flag misfires not asserted: _missing-interactions.json claims "Malphite bypasses stacking resistances (Granite Shield (P))" (a shield with a percentHealth flag, not resistance bypass) and calls Thunderclap an auto-attack reset (Riot's text does not say reset — I described the aftershock cone instead, which is in the text). Rumble's own Scrap Shield "knockup"/"terrain" flags and The Equalizer's "terrain" flag remain misfires and are not used here.
